transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Lucas Patel, Priya Rao (Redwood) — Ibrahim Noor, Elena Park, Sam Ortiz, Rui Zhang (Synergetic Labs)

Summary: initial discovery about integrating Redwood into Synergetic's inference path. Focus on deciding between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, gateway/proxy footprint and rate-limit model, and observability hooks for tracing and cost allocation.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE. Lucas is our SE, Priya is on solutions. Ibrahim, do you want to kick off with what you're trying to solve?
[00:20] Ibrahim (Synergetic): Yeah, thanks. We run an internal platform that serving recommendations and some conversational features for customers, and latency at tail is a problem. We're exploring Redwood because we need predictable cost and the ability to run on-prem for some regulated clients.
[00:36] Elena: Also want better observability — breaking down per-team token spend and seeing which routes spike.
[00:44] Lucas (Redwood): Totally. To frame — Redwood has three paths: Hosted API for quick time-to-value, Dedicated reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for data residency. Each has different trade-offs on latency, control, and cost.
[01:05] Sam (Synergetic): Quick question — if we start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated, how seamless is that? Does the SDK change?
[01:12] Maya: Good question. The API is consistent; SDKs are the same. You can pin model versions and rollout policies independent of underlying infra. There are config knobs when you move to Dedicated, like autoscale policies and burst capacity settings.
[01:30] Rui (Security): On Private: what about KMS/HSM and audit logs? We have strict requirements — keys must be customer-managed.
[01:38] Priya: We support customer KMS integration for Private, and audit logs with retention options. We'll pull the SOC 2 and network architecture diagrams for you.
[01:50] [crosstalk] Ibrahim: Great. Also do you support SAML SSO for admin console?
[01:55] Maya: Yes, SSO and RBAC are available across Dedicated and Private consoles. Hosted accounts also support enterprise SSO for workspace-level control.

[02:20] Topics: SDKs & integrations
[02:25] Lucas: Walkthrough of SDK patterns — simple REST, node/python SDKs, and a gateway proxy pattern commonly used when teams want request routing, auth translation, and central rate-limiting in front of Redwood.
[02:40] Elena: We're heavy on LangChain and LlamaIndex. How much work is plugging Redwood in? Any shim layers?
[02:48] Lucas: We have examples for LangChain connectors and a LlamaIndex-compatible DocumentStore flow. Note: sometimes LlamaIndex is transcribed in our docs as "Lama Index" — small typo, but the connectors are compatible. If you use the LangChain agents, you can swap the OpenAI-ish client for Redwood's client with minimal changes.
[03:10] Sam: Are there rate-limit semantics we should be aware of for agents that do many parallel calls?
[03:16] Lucas: Two pieces — per-token throttling and request concurrency. On Hosted we enforce default global quotas; you can request increased quotas. On Dedicated you control the pool size and autoscale, so concurrency behaves predictably. With Private, you manage infra; Redwood's control plane still provides usage telemetry and suggested batching configs.
[03:40] Ibrahim: How does KV cache / prefix caching work? We want to reduce repeated context costs.
[03:47] Priya: We recommend prefix caching on repeated prompts and continuum batching — our runtime manages KV cache between requests when clients supply session IDs. Note that some of the caching language in auto transcripts shows "K V cash" — small OCR funnyness.

[04:10] [10m mark] Technical constraints and POC ask
[04:12] Elena: For a POC we'd like the gateway to do auth + rate-limit + routing to different models for A/B. Can Redwood gateway handle per-tenant routing?
[04:22] Lucas: Yes, routing by policy (latency, cost, region) is supported. The typical pattern: a lightweight edge proxy handles auth, request shaping, and then calls Redwood with a tenant header. The control plane can route to a cheaper quantized model variant when latency isn't critical.
[04:40] Sam: Any dogfooding patterns for LangChain heavy workloads? We run a lot of small LLM calls inside chains that create fan-out.
[04:48] Lucas: For fan-out-heavy workloads, we recommend batching at the SDK layer and using async clients. We also have suggestions to restructure chains so that only necessary calls are dispatched, and to leverage local caching for embeddings.

[05:20] Observability hooks and cost attribution
[05:24] Priya: On the observability side, Redwood provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route trace ids, and a tracing hook so you can join traces with your existing APM. You can export metrics via Prometheus or send export to your monitoring system.
[05:38] Rui: Do you emit request IDs that map back to our internal tenant ids for billing?
[05:42] Maya: Yes — you can pass tenant metadata and we'll surface per-tenant dashboards. There are also exportable CSVs for cost reconciliation.

[06:00] Security & compliance discussion
[06:05] Rui: For Private/on-prem, how isolated is the control plane? We want the option of air-gapped with scheduled pull updates.
[06:12] Priya: Our Private deployment has an option for an air-gap install where the customer controls the control plane network. For hybrid you can have a customer-managed control plane with occasional syncs; we'll share the install doc.
[06:28] Rui: Data retention and redact rules? We need to ensure PII is never stored beyond X days unless flagged.
[06:34] Maya: We offer configurable retention policies and an option to not persist user inputs in Hosted for regulated accounts. We'll send the data flow diagram.

[07:00] Cost modeling and Dedicated details
[07:05] Maya: For Dedicated, we provide reserved capacity contracts. You can configure autoscale min/max, plus burst pools for sudden spikes. We'll produce a TCO comparing Hosted egress and token costs vs Dedicated fixed + utilization assumptions.
[07:20] Ibrahim: If we use Dedicated but want region fallback to Hosted for burst, is that supported?
[07:25] Lucas: Yes, we support smart routing with fallback to compatible hosted model variants if Dedicated pool is saturated. You can set fallback policies per route.

[07:50] POC design ideas
[07:52] Sam: For the POC, propose a small subset of routes — 2 realtime chat routes and 1 batch embed job. We want to validate latency tail and cost per 100k tokens.
[07:59] Maya: Sounds good. We'll draft an experiment plan: test scenarios, success criteria (p95 latency under 350ms, and cost reduction target 20% vs current infra).

[08:20] Questions raised by Synergetic
[08:24] Elena: How do you handle model upgrades and rollouts to avoid regressions?
[08:28] Lucas: Rollouts supported: canary, gradual, and automatic fallback on degraded quality or latency. We also have eval hooks tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions before flipping traffic.
[08:45] Ibrahim: Do you support custom quantized model uploads?
[08:49] Priya: We support model onboarding for compatible formats; our Research team works with customers on quantization profiles. We'll need a sample model binary for evaluation.

[09:10] Rough wrap and recap
[09:15] Maya: Recap — Redwood will: (1) share SOC2 + network and KMS docs, (2) provide Dedicated vs Hosted TCO with burst pricing, (3) prep LangChain/LlamaIndex quickstart repo and gateway proxy example, (4) draft POC plan. Synergetic will share traffic histograms and quota spreadsheet.
[09:35] Ibrahim: Excellent. Also we'll review the competitor notes you shared. A couple of our teams are benchmarking Anthropic and OpenAI.
[09:45] Maya: Understood — we'll include notes on comparative latency/cost for similar workloads.

[10:00] End

Notes about transcript quality: There are a few transcription artefacts — speaker labels occasionally generic (Speaker 1), some product names are slightly off ("Lama index"), and acronyms (K V cache) get spaced. Intent preserved.
